misses.reason: tests/test_docs.py now recomputes the never-reproduced sentence, but the README and REPORT §2b noise-floor figures (21 and 26 points), the claim that had gone stale at 17, still have no check.
tests/test_docs.py recomputes the pool and never-reproduced counts from receipts, but the re-transcribed 21- and 26-point floor in README.md and evals/REPORT.md has no recomputing test.
The new _arm_counts in tests/test_docs.py pools every receipt from raw rows and skips unevaluable ones but not the PLAN_ONLY list that _pool applies for §4j's excluded sample.
The DreamBench row in docs/RELATED-WORK.md still says 'What no benchmark reports' about stale detection, unscoped, though the same page now admits other work measures it.
docs/GETTING-STARTED.md states the merge-commit requirement, but the branch commits stamped in okl-drift.json only survive if the live repo settings still force a merge commit.

`ci/check-agent-neutral.py` matches surfaces on unnormalised text with `[- ]`, so a mention wrapped across lines passes, against the lesson's normalise-whitespace fix; `docs/decisions/2026-10-05-records-not-an-ontology-store.md:81` is one.

Unlabelled line-wrapped mentions remain at `docs/decisions/2026-10-10-org-lessons-ledger-repo.md:20` ("The Stop\nhook") and `docs/decisions/2026-10-05-records-not-an-ontology-store.md:81` ("a prompt\nhook"), and `ci/check-agent-neutral.py` cannot see them.

The _Backend docstring in src/okl/store.py now promises aliases are matchable, but the shared _backend_conformance in tests/test_okl.py never searches an alias, so the new test runs on the SQLite fixture only.
README.md adds the 'one record in twenty' claim, but no drift rule or check in okl-drift.json or the tests compares it with core.COMMON_WORD_SHARE, so changing the constant turns nothing red.

In core.py `record`/`_supersede`, a retraction on the old id is overwritten with 'superseded' while an already-held new id stays live, and seed.py `_held_under_old_names` skips team-superseded old records, so `okl seed` recreates them live under the new id.

core.py `lessons_without_triggers` now resolves old names through `current_pack`, but the identical `parts[1] in bundled` check in src/okl/review.py `unchecked` was missed, so old-named pack records silently count as the store's own.
tests/test_docs.py holds figures to receipts, but the new docs/DEVELOPING.md claims (postgres:17.6, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, soft-pass) have no check or rule in okl-drift.json tying them to ci.yml.
.github/workflows/ci.yml asserts its git allowlist has 'only forms that cannot write', but no test enforces it and git log/show accept --output=<file>.
ci.yml's review step stays green when the secret is missing and review-agent.sh exits 0 on an unparseable reply, so whether a review really ran on a PR must be confirmed from the live run's output.

`_workflow_reads_pin` in src/okl/cli/install.py finds the step by the literal name `- name: Install okl`, so a kept workflow with that step renamed that still reads the pin is reported as not reading it and its pin stops moving, a failed match that looks like a real negative.
REPORT §4ad says the backend contract and conformance suite gain the rebuild case, but the _Backend docstring and _backend_conformance do not, and tests/test_stem.py covers SQLite only.
src/okl/scaffold/evals/run_evals.py now exits 2 for placeholder or empty cases, but a missing cases file still prints 'Nothing to measure' and returns 0, so CI passes having checked nothing.

`src/okl/cli/parser.py` and `docs/COMMANDS.md` say doctor writes nothing, but `_interest_lines` opens a Store whose `init_schema` upgrades an older store or creates tables in an empty Postgres; only the docstring admits the exception.

CONTRIBUTING.md documents merge-commits-only and why, and src/okl/drift.py does read %ct, but allow_squash_merge/allow_rebase_merge are live GitHub settings the repo cannot show, so the author should confirm they are off.
